'''Xiaodong Wang''' (born 1963) is a Chinese-American [[biochemist]] best known for his work with [[apoptosis]], which is the normal physiologic process of [[programmed cell death]].

== Early life and education ==
Wang was born in [[Wuhan]], [[China]] in 1963, and was raised in [[Xinxiang]], [[Henan]] by his grandparents. His family was relatively well-educated. His grandfather was a [[Secondary school|high school]] [[English language|English]] [[teacher]], his grandmother a [[primary school]] teacher, and his great uncle a [[biology]] [[professor]]. His primary and secondary coincided with the [[Cultural Revolution]], and he only started high school in 1978 at a top high school in Henan.<ref name="autobio"/><ref name="pnas">{{cite journal |last1=Zagorski |first1=Nick |title=Profile of Xiaodong Wang |journal=[[Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences of the United States of America]] |date=2006 |volume=103 |issue=1 |pages=7–9 |doi=10.1073/pnas.0509187103 |pmid=16380419 |pmc=1324996 |doi-access=free|bibcode=2006PNAS..103....7Z }}</ref>

He entered the [[Beijing Normal University]] in 1980,<ref name="autobio"/> majoring in [[biology]], and completed 4 years later.<ref name="nibs">{{cite web |title=王晓东博士 |url=http://www.nibs.ac.cn/yjsjyimgshow.php?cid=5&sid=6&id=779 |publisher=National Institute of Biological Sciences, Beijing |access-date=October 19, 2023 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20231019064822/http://www.nibs.ac.cn/yjsjyimgshow.php?cid=5&sid=6&id=779 |archive-date=October 19, 2023 |language=zh}}</ref> His [[Undergraduate education|undergraduate]] thesis supervisor, Shaobai Xue, introduced him to [[cell biology]] and [[biochemistry]], and prompted him to pursue [[Postgraduate education|postgraduate]] studies in biochemistry.<ref name="autobio"/>

Through the government-sponsored Chinese-US Biochemistry Examination and Application (CUSBEA) program, the biochemistry counterpart to [[CUSPEA]], Wang went to the [[University of Texas Southwestern Medical Center]] in 1985 for his [[Doctor of Philosophy|PhD]].<ref name="autobio"/> The CUSBEA program was initiated by the biochemist [[Ray Wu]] at [[Cornell University]] and lasted from 1982 to 1989.<ref>{{cite journal |last1=Chang |first1=Zengyi |title=The CUSBEA program: Twenty years after |journal=[[IUBMB Life]] |date=2009 |volume=61 |issue=6 |pages=555–565 |doi=10.1002/iub.218 |pmid=19472190 |doi-access=free}}</ref><ref>{{cite journal |last1=Gu |first1=Xiaocheng |title=Ray Wu and the CUSBEA Program |journal=Science in China Series C: Life Sciences |date=2009 |volume=52 |issue=2 |pages=125–127 |doi=10.1007/s11427-009-0020-9 |pmid=19277521 |url=https://link.springer.com/article/10.1007/s11427-009-0020-9 |access-date=October 19, 2023|url-access=subscription }}</ref> He graduated in 1991.<ref name="nibs"/>

== Career ==
After obtaining his [[Doctor of Philosophy|PhD]], Wang moved to the research group of [[Joseph L. Goldstein]] and [[Michael Stuart Brown]], also at the [[University of Texas Southwestern Medical Center]] (UTSW) as a [[Postdoctoral researcher|postdoctoral fellow]]. He joined the Department of [[Biochemistry]] of [[Emory University]] in 1995 as an [[assistant professor]], then returned to UTSW a year later as an assistant professor at its Department of Biochemistry. He was promoted to [[associate professor]] in 1999.<ref name="nibs"/> In 2001, Wang was appointed the George L. MacGregor Distinguished Chair in [[Biomedical Science]]s.<ref name="prospectus">{{cite book |title=BeiGene, Ltd. Global Offering Prospectus |date=July 30, 2018 |publisher=[[BeiGene]] |page=323 |url=https://www1.hkexnews.hk/listedco/listconews/sehk/2018/0730/ltn20180730005.pdf |access-date=October 20, 2023 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20231020161710/https://www1.hkexnews.hk/listedco/listconews/sehk/2018/0730/ltn20180730005.pdf |archive-date=October 20, 2023 |chapter=DIRECTORS AND SENIOR MANAGEMENT}}</ref>

Wang became an investigator at the [[Howard Hughes Medical Institute]] in 1997.<ref>{{cite web |title=Xiaodong Wang, PhD |url=https://www.hhmi.org/scientists/xiaodong-wang |publisher=[[Howard Hughes Medical Institute]] |access-date=October 20, 2023 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20231020162530/https://www.hhmi.org/scientists/xiaodong-wang |archive-date=October 20, 2023}}</ref>

Since 2003, Wang has been an investigator at the National Institute of Biological Sciences, Beijing (NIBS). In 2010, he ended all his positions in the [[United States]] and returned to [[China]] to take up the role of director of NIBS.<ref name="prospectus"/>

Wang co-founded two [[biotechnology]] companies: Joyant Pharmaceuticals in 2004 and [[BeiGene]], co-founded with [[John V. Oyler|John Oyler]],<ref name="Wright">{{cite news |last1=Wright |first1=Rob |title=How — And Why — John Oyler Built BeiGene |url=https://www.lifescienceleader.com/doc/how-and-why-john-oyler-built-beigene-0001 |access-date=26 September 2023 |work=Life Science Leader |date=1 November 2019}}</ref> in 2010.<ref>{{cite web |title=BeiGene |url=https://www.forbes.com/companies/beigene/?sh=14523211c510 |work=[[Forbes]] |access-date=October 21, 2023 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20231021151620/https://www.forbes.com/companies/beigene/?sh=14523211c510 |archive-date=October 21, 2023}}</ref> He currently chairs the Scientific Advisory Board of BeiGene.<ref>{{cite web |title=Xiaodong Wang, Ph.D. |url=https://www.beigene.com/leadership/xiaodong-wang-ph-d/ |publisher=BeiGene |access-date=October 18, 2023 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20231018063026/https://www.beigene.com/leadership/xiaodong-wang-ph-d/ |archive-date=October 18, 2023}}</ref>

Wang chaired the Science Committee of the Future Science Prize in 2017, and currently sits on the committee.<ref>{{cite web |title=Xiaodong WANG |url=http://www.futureprize.org/en/people/81.html |publisher=Future Science Prize |access-date=October 31, 2023 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20231031073155/http://www.futureprize.org/en/people/81.html |archive-date=October 31, 2023}}</ref>

== Research ==
Wang's research on [[apoptosis]] began accidentally when he was a [[Postdoctoral researcher|postdoctoral fellow]] at the research group of [[Joseph L. Goldstein]] and [[Michael Stuart Brown]] at the [[University of Texas Southwestern Medical Center]]. Apoptosis is a form of [[programmed cell death]], which is the mechanisms that [[Cell (biology)|cells]] use kill themselves. Brown and Goldstein were at the time studying the [[transcriptional regulation]] of the [[LDL receptor|low-density lipoprotein (LDL) receptor]] in response to [[cholesterol]] level. One of the regulatory mechanisms was through the activation of [[Sterol regulatory element-binding protein|SREBP]], a [[protein]] that regulates the [[Transcription (biology)|manufacturing]] of [[mRNA]] from [[gene]]s coding for  proteins that import and synthesize cholesterol. SREBP bound to [[nuclear envelope]] and [[endoplasmic reticulum]] membranes, and had to be cleaved to be activated.<ref>{{cite journal |title=SREBPs: activators of the complete program of cholesterol and fatty acid synthesis in the liver |journal=[[Journal of Clinical Investigation]] |date=2002 |volume=109 |issue=9 |pages=1125–1131 |doi=10.1172/JCI15593 |pmid=11994399 |pmc=150968 |doi-access=free |last1=Horton |first1=Jay D. |last2=Goldstein |first2=Joseph L. |last3=Brown |first3=Michael S. }}</ref>

In 1995, Wang reported a protein in [[hamster]]s believed to be the one that cleaved SREBP. However, he also found that the human counterpart of this hamster protein was CPP32, which itself was related to one of the first proteins shown to be involved in initiating apoptosis.<ref>{{cite journal |first1=Xiaodong |last1=Wang |first2=Jih-tung |last2=Pai |first3=Elizabeth A. |last3=Wiedenfeld |first4=Julio C. |last4=Medina |first5=Clive A. |last5=Slaughter |first6=Joseph L. |last6=Goldstein |first7=Michael S. |last7=Brown |authorlink6=Joseph L. Goldstein |authorlink7=Michael Stuart Brown |title=Purification of an Interleukin-1β Converting Enzyme-related Cysteine Protease That Cleaves Sterol Regulatory Element-binding Proteins between the Leucine Zipper and Transmembrane Domains |journal=[[Journal of Biological Chemistry]] |date=1995 |volume=270 |issue=30 |pages=18044–18050 |doi=10.1074/jbc.270.30.18044 |pmid=7629113 |doi-access=free}}</ref> The CPP32 protein was officially renamed [[caspase 3]] the following year.<ref>{{cite journal |first1=Emad S. |last1=Alnemri |first2=David J. |last2=Livingston |first3=Donald W. |last3=Nicholson |first4=Guy |last4=Salvesen |first5=Nancy A. |last5=Thornberry |first6=Winnie W. |last6=Wong |first7=Junying |last7=Yuan |authorlink1=Emad Alnemri |authorlink4=Guy Salvesen |authorlink5=Nancy Thornberry |authorlink7=Junying Yuan |title=Human ICE/CED-3 Protease Nomenclature |journal=[[Cell (journal)|Cell]] |date=1996 |volume=87 |issue=2 |pages=171 |doi=10.1016/s0092-8674(00)81334-3 |pmid=8861900 |doi-access=free }}</ref>

Breakthrough came during Wang's one year at [[Emory University]], when he developed a cell-free, ''[[in vitro]]'' system that replicated the activation of caspase 3 and the initiation of apoptosis.<ref name="pnas"/> Using this system, his group characterized the proteins required for starting apoptosis, including [[cytochrome c]],<ref>{{cite journal |first1=Xuesong |last1=Liu |first2=Caryn Naekyung |last2=Kim |first3=Jie |last3=Yang |first4=Ronald |last4=Jemmerson |first5=Xiaodong |last5=Wang |title=Induction of Apoptotic Program in Cell-Free Extracts: Requirement for dATP and Cytochrome c |journal=Cell |date=1996 |volume=86 |issue=1 |pages=147–157 |doi=10.1016/s0092-8674(00)80085-9 |pmid=8689682 |doi-access=free }}</ref> [[Bcl-2]],<ref>{{cite journal |first1=Jie |last1=Yang |first2=Xuesong |last2=Liu |first3=Kapil |last3=Bhalla |first4=Caryn Naekyung |last4=Kim |first5=Ana Maria |last5=Ibrado |first6=Jiyang |last6=Cai |first7=Tsung-I |last7=Peng |first8=Dean P. |last8=Jones |first9=Xiaodong |last9=Wang |title=Prevention of Apoptosis by Bcl-2: Release of Cytochrome c from Mitochondria Blocked |journal=[[Science (journal)|Science]] |date=1997 |volume=275 |issue=5303 |pages=1129–1132 |doi=10.1126/science.275.5303.1129 |pmid=9027314 |url=https://www.science.org/doi/10.1126/science.275.5303.1129 |access-date=October 30, 2023|url-access=subscription }}</ref> [[APAF1]],<ref>{{cite journal |last1=Zou |first1=Hua |last2=Henzel |first2=William J. |last3=Liu |first3=Xuesong |last4=Lutschg |first4=Alexis |last5=Wang |first5=Xiaodong |date=1997 |title=Apaf-1, a human protein homologous to C. elegans CED-4, participates in cytochrome c-dependent activation of caspase-3 |journal=Cell |volume=90 |issue=3 |pages=405–413 |issn=0092-8674 |pmid=9267021 |doi=10.1016/s0092-8674(00)80501-2 |s2cid=18105320 |doi-access=free }}</ref> and [[Caspase-9|pro-caspase-9]].<ref name="pmid9390557">{{cite journal |first1=Peng |last1=Li |first2=Deepak |last2=Nijhawan |first3=Imawati |last3=Budihardjo |first4=Srinivasa M. |last4=Srinivasula |first5=Manzoor |last5=Ahmad |first6=Emad S. |last6=Alnemri |first7=Xiaodong |last7=Wang |title=Cytochrome c and dATP-Dependent Formation of Apaf-1/Caspase-9 Complex Initiates an Apoptotic Protease Cascade |journal=Cell |date=1997 |volume=91 |issue=4 |pages=479–489 |doi=10.1016/s0092-8674(00)80434-1 |pmid=9390557 |doi-access=free }}</ref>

In 1997, his group reported the activation steps of apoptosis: Bcl-2 regulates the release of cytochrome c from the [[Mitochondrion|mitochondria]] to the [[cytosol]], then cytochrome c binds to APAF1 and forms a protein complex called the [[apoptosome]]. The apoptosome recruits and cleaves procaspase-9 to the active form caspase-9, which in turn cleaves procaspase-3 to the active caspase 3.<ref name="pmid9390557"/>

Apart from apoptosis, Wang also discovered the [[necroptosis]] pathway, which is the programmed form of [[necrosis]] and another way that a [[Cell (biology)|cell]] [[programmed cell death|kills]] itself. He established the role of [[RIPK3]] and the [[Mixed lineage kinase domain like pseudokinase|MLKL]] protein in necroptosis.<ref>{{cite journal |first1=Liming |last1=Sun |first2=Huayi |last2=Wang |first3=Zhigao |last3=Wang |first4=Sudan |last4=He |first5=She |last5=Chen |first6=Daohong |last6=Liao |first7=Lai |last7=Wang |first8=Jiacong |last8=Yan |first9=Weilong |last9=Liu |first10=Xiaoguang |last10=Lei |first11=Xiaodong |last11=Wang |title=Mixed Lineage Kinase Domain-like Protein Mediates Necrosis Signaling Downstream of RIP3 Kinase |journal=Cell |date=2012 |volume=148 |issue=1–2 |pages=213–227 |doi=10.1016/j.cell.2011.11.031 |pmid=22265413 |doi-access=free }}</ref>
